paragraphs.source_en: In late May of the fifth year of Keichō, the tiresome rainy season finally ended. The sky was deep blue, and the intermittent chirring of cicadas drifted from somewhere unseen. Kōdai-in, living in retirement at Sanbongi, sent someone to Hon'ami Kōetsu's house to ask him to name a newly fired tea bowl by Chōjirō. Kōetsu started when he saw the maid who had been sent. Her face seemed familiar, yet he could not remember who she was.
